title: rpg-classic party roster
description: One player-side roster: the single source of truth for what a companion IS in a fight, the player-side mirror of eve.rpgc.enemy. The engine has no content type for this (Party.cpp is a runtime container of already-registered actors, it carries no numbers), so nothing rejects a roster whose member has no element or a misspelled skill id — the semantic gate and the cross-document gate are the only readers, exactly like eve.rpgc.battle. `combat` mirrors the enemy block field for field because both sides are fed to the same resolver in lib/rpgc_battle.nut. `art` + `grade` are the designed runtime projection of a martial art's grade into concrete skill ids (docs/06-game-design.md §2.4): available moves = union(grades[1..grade].skills + ultimates) of that art document, and `skills[]` lists the moves that belong to no art. `sprite` is optional on purpose: the workflow ships CC0 monster art but no hero sheet, and a required field would force authors to name a file that does not exist. The roster size is NOT capped here: `maxBattleAllySlots` in RpgcSystems is the only copy of that number, and a schema `maxItems` would return before the semantic gate that reads it, making the gate unreachable. `startingItems` is the opening bag, and it lives HERE rather than in `rules` because it is a roster fact: the engine has no "what the party starts with" concept either, so lib/rpgc_items.nut is the only reader. `itemId` is an outbound reference to an item document (gate layer 3); `count` is bounded at 1 by the schema, so the semantic gate deliberately does not repeat that check — it only refuses an id it cannot read and a duplicate, neither of which the schema can see.
